title: Tyndale error_detection_rules record
description: Narrative policy/rule text that gets embedded. NCCI/MUE TABULAR lookups live in Postgres, not here — only the narrative reasoning goes into Qdrant. EXTENDED 2026-08-22 (Brock's 38 §3, accepted): rule_class splits provider-coding rules from payer-adjudication / legal-protection / pricing rules; applicable_codes is required ONLY for provider_coding (payer-side rules match on adjudication facts, not codes); responsible_party attributes the finding.

rule_type.description: Provider-coding types (ncci_ptp…phantom_charge) + payer-side adjudication types (2026-08-22 extension).

applicable_codes.description: Codes this rule applies to. REQUIRED for rule_class=provider_coding; optional (allowed, not required) for every other class.

payer.description: Null for universal rules; otherwise the payer name.

narrative_text.description: The policy text that gets embedded (paraphrased, not verbatim).

structured_rule_id.description: Optional pointer to the Postgres structured NCCI/MUE table; null for non-tabular rules.

rule_class.description: What kind of rule this is. provider_coding REQUIRES applicable_codes; the other classes may omit them (they match on adjudication facts / legal posture / pricing benchmarks).

responsible_party.description: Who a violation of this rule implicates — drives finding attribution on the card.

examples.narrative_text: A comprehensive metabolic panel and a complete blood count are commonly reported together and are not a bundled pair under NCCI; however, billing both with a panel component that overlaps (e.g., a basic metabolic panel on the same day) is a procedure-to-procedure conflict and the column-two code is denied unless a clinically appropriate modifier applies.

When the EOB applies a deductible to a service after the member's accumulated deductible has already been met for the plan year, the member responsibility is overstated. Compare the EOB's applied-deductible amount against the member's year-to-date accumulator position; a deductible charge that exceeds the remaining deductible is an adjudication error and the claim should be reprocessed.
